correctness.rationale: First-force degree bound gives |B|>=2k-1; at equality the first force must be from a deleted-edge endpoint. For d<k the subsequent black neighborhood-with-hole has two white neighbors at every black non-endpoint and stalls, while an intact 2k interval forces using only distance-k edges. For d=k the first force turns its neighborhood into an intact 2k interval, which forces in the opposite direction using other distance-k edges. All 2(2k-1) distinct equality cases follow from first-move necessity. Standalone exhaustive direct simulator independently verified 80 parameter combinations and 341272 candidate configurations.

value.rationale: Single-edge resilience is a natural structural refinement of zero forcing on circulants and of general edge-spread theory. The result gives a sharp metric criterion (only maximal-distance chords are fragile), the complete exceptional minimum seed geometry, and an n-independent count 4k-2 for an infinite two-parameter family. This resolves a meaningful sensitivity classification not implied by the scalar graph-power zero-forcing number.
